battle.name: 菲律賓革命
battle.theater: 馬尼拉都會區與中呂宋
battle.brief: 一八九六年八月二十三日，蓋蒂普南在馬尼拉北郊發動武裝起事，呂宋中部的武裝農民以冷刃與繳獲步槍攻擊西班牙殖民軍，鄉村堡壘與游擊隊撐了四個月。交戰雙方靠山炮、連發步槍與刺刀分勝負，戰役裡並無加特林機槍；這件六管速射武器要到三年後美軍遠征時才踏上前線，作為炮兵與步兵之間的火力銜接。

kit.history: 六根管子用人力轉動。它的後坐力分散在六次上，所以能壓住一個師。

countries: 交戰一方是西班牙王國及其駐菲律賓總督府，另一方是蓋蒂普南所領導的革命軍。西班牙方面以馬尼拉都會區為中樞，總督卡米洛·波拉維哈一八九六年七月到任，隨即在首都宣布戒嚴、查禁地方武裝；城防由數個步兵營、常備炮兵、工兵與海軍登陸隊組成，另有土著士兵組成、受西班牙軍官指揮的輔助部隊與「民警團」在鄉間巡邏，教堂僧侶的武裝組織和教會警衛隊在部分城鎮與修道院據點擔任守備，教會的土地與地產利益令教團在起事初期成為西班牙方面的助力。維薩亞群島與棉蘭老方面另派有常備軍與分遣隊，同樣由總督府調度。革命軍以「蓋蒂普南」（他加祿語：最崇高最受尊崇之愛國子民會）為核心，一八九二年八月由安德烈斯·博尼法西奧在馬尼拉唐多區創立，最初人數極少，到起事前自報約三萬人，分設八個以上分會，覆蓋馬尼拉、布拉干、卡維特、邦板牙、巴丹、八打雁、內湖、塔亞巴斯、新怡詩夏與三描禮士等中呂宋地區；其後把總會改組成「蓋蒂普南協會」，下設議事、軍務、司法三個機關，戰時在鄉村以「阿利卡班」取代西班牙的市政廳，實際接管稅收、徵兵與糧食徵集，成為與殖民政府並行的另一套行政系統。西班牙之外，馬尼拉與香港的宣傳運動者、以及南下的華人革命團體構成外圍的支援與補給；美國遠征軍直到一八九八年因西班牙—美國戰爭的結果才介入，因此不屬於本場戰役的交戰方。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the Kingdom of Spain together with its Captaincy General of the Philippines; the other was the revolutionary movement led by the Katipunan. On the Spanish side the centre of gravity was metropolitan Manila. Governor-General Camilo Polavieja took office in July 1896, immediately proclaimed martial law in the capital and suppressed local armed organisations. The city was defended by several infantry battalions, the standing artillery, engineers and a naval landing force, supported by auxiliary units of native soldiers under Spanish officers and by a civic constabulary patrolling the countryside; armed ecclesiastical bodies and church guards held a number of towns and convent strongpoints, and since the Church's land and estate interests made the religious orders an asset to the Spanish side in the first months of the revolt. Separate permanent garrisons and detachments in the Visayas and in Mindanao were tasked from the same headquarters. The insurgents were organised around the Katipunan — in Tagalog, the most exalted and most honoured association of the children of the nation — founded by Andrés Bonifacio in the Tondo district of Manila in August 1892 from very few members, claiming by the eve of the rising to have some thirty thousand adherents divided into more than eight chapters covering Manila, Bulacan, Cavite, Pampanga, Bataan, Batangas, Laguna, Tayabas, Nueva Ecija and parts of Zambales. The general assembly was later reorganised as the Kawanihan ng Katipunan with deliberative, military and judicial organs, and in the villages the alikaban replaced the Spanish municipal council, actually taking over taxation, recruitment and the collection of food, so that a second administration ran parallel to the colonial one. Outside the islands the propagandists working in Manila and Hong Kong, and the Chinese revolutionary groups that had moved south, formed the outer ring of support and supply. The American expedition entered the picture only in 1898, as a result of the Spanish–American War, and is therefore not a belligerent in this campaign.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊。革命軍這邊的核心是安德烈斯·博尼法西奧（一八六三至一八九七），他做過倉庫管理與市政雇員，參與過一八九二年成立的菲律賓聯盟，隨後另立蓋蒂普南，把殖民當局的貪污、苛捐與教產爭議寫成宣傳小冊子散發，認定請願道路已盡，決心以武裝起事取代陳情。宣誓儀式初期由特奧多里科·雷耶斯主持；埃米利奧·哈辛托是起事後的參謀長，也是「卡蒂利亞·德·蓋蒂普南」十四條綱領的作者，主張互助團結、成員平等與把教產歸還佃農，馬里亞諾·龐塞負責在港募款與印行刊物，胡利奧·納克皮爾在報紙上發表革命主張。宣傳派的領袖有格拉西亞諾·洛佩斯·哈埃納、多明戈·法蘭科、馬塞洛·H·德爾·皮拉爾與馬里亞諾·龐塞；何塞·黎剎被控為蓋蒂普南成員，於一八九六年十二月三十日在巴岡巴揚被處決，遺體葬於帕科公墓，後世尊之為民族英雄。一八九七年五月，馬尼拉代表在特耶羅斯會議另立埃米利奧·阿吉納爾多為最高領袖，博尼法西奧退往馬拉貢坦，同年五月十日與兄弟普羅科皮奧、瓦卡利奧在馬格塞塞被西班牙軍隊處決。西班牙方面，總督波拉維哈在馬尼拉組織反擊，任命將軍阿古斯丁·德·萊加斯皮率領先鋒隊；萊加斯皮在馬尼拉近郊交戰中受傷後由拉蒙·卡夫雷拉接手，先鋒隊與自維薩亞抵達的援軍逐省收復卡維特與八打雁；一八九七年四月接任的總督費爾南多·普里莫·德·里維拉改以掃帚式政策清剿，再以《比亞克—巴塔特條約》與阿吉納爾多議和。地方一線還有卡維特的馬里亞諾·特里亞斯與馬西莫·維奧拉、布拉干的格列戈里奧·德爾·皮拉爾、馬尼拉的迭戈·林戈與皮奧·瓦連蘇埃拉等指揮官。
peopleEn: The decisive figures on the insurgent side included Andrés Bonifacio (1863–1897), a warehouse clerk and municipal employee who had belonged to the Liga Filipina founded in 1892 and had then founded the Katipunan, scattering leaflets on colonial corruption, ruinous taxation and the dispute over friar lands; he had concluded that the road of petition was closed and that the movement had to answer with arms. The initiation rites were at first administered by Teodorico Reyes. Emilio Jacinto became chief of staff after the rising and wrote the fourteen precepts of the Kartilya ng Katipunan, arguing for mutual aid, equality among members and the return of the estates to those who worked them; Mariano Ponce handled money and printing in Hong Kong, and Julio Nakpil carried the case in the press. The Propaganda Movement leadership was Graciano López Jaena, Domingo Franco, Marcelo H. del Pilar and Mariano Ponce. José Rizal, accused of being a member of the Katipunan, was executed at Bagumbayan on 30 December 1896 and buried in Paco Park; later generations honoured him as a national hero. In May 1897 the Manila delegates at the Tejeros Convention set Emilio Aguinaldo up as supreme, Bonifacio withdrew to Maragondon, and on 10 May he and his brothers Procopio and Valentino were shot by a Spanish firing squad at Magsaysay. On the Spanish side Governor-General Polavieja organised the counter-offensive at Manila and entrusted it to General Agustín de Legazpi; after Legazpi was wounded in the fighting near the capital the command passed to Ramón Cabrera, and the vanguard columns, reinforced from the Visayas, recovered Cavite and the province of Batangas one province at a time. Fernando Primo de Rivera, who took over as governor-general in April 1897, switched to a policy of sweeping executions and then negotiated with Aguinaldo under the Pact of Biak-na-Bato. At local level the commanders included Mariano Trias and Máximo Viola in Cavite, Gregorio del Pilar in Bulacan, and Diego Linggo and Pío Valenzuela in Manila.
kits: 卡面這件加特林機槍，是李察·加特林一八六〇年構思、一八六一年做出原型的手搖多管速射武器：六根槍管由人力搖柄帶動旋轉，後坐力分散在六次射擊上，射速因此遠高於單管後膛槍。美國陸軍在一八六四至一八六五年大量採購，一八七九年之後定型為七點六二毫米口徑、三腳架架設的制式槍械，作戰射速約每分鐘一百發，彈藥用百發裝的圓形彈鼓，一門槍要四至六人操作。但必須老實說明：一八九六年的這場革命裡，西班牙殖民軍與蓋蒂普南都沒有使用加特林機槍。西班牙方面的常備與要塞速射武器是七點六五毫米毛瑟系連發步槍、貝克式步槍以及舊式雷明登轉輪步槍，火力骨幹是十二、十六厘米野戰炮與山炮，河海方向靠汽艇與砲艦支援。革命軍的裝備以冷刃（波羅刀、桑加特刀）加繳獲的毛瑟與雷明登步槍為主；起事前購買的四萬支步槍與四萬發子彈因英國海軍在港外扣押運武裝船「浩生號」（Kowshing）而從未到岸，起義軍雖在馬尼拉近郊繳獲過數門西班牙山炮，卻缺乏配套炮手與備件。真正讓加特林機槍踏上菲律賓土地的是三年後的事：一八九九年美軍遠征後的菲美戰爭中，美軍炮兵攜帶三腳架式加特林機槍，用於掩護步兵沿道路與稻田推進，也用在伊穆斯、馬拉邦與布拉干一役的正面進攻。換言之，這張卡上的武器代表的是下一場戰爭的火力形態，而不是一八九六年八月的實況。
kitsEn: The Gatling gun on the card was Richard Gatling's hand-cranked multi-barrel weapon, conceived in 1860 and brought to a working prototype in 1861: six barrels are rotated by a hand crank, so the recoil is spread over six separate shots and the rate of fire far exceeds that of any single-shot breech gun. The United States Army bought the weapon in quantity in 1864 and 1865, and from 1879 it was standardised as a .30 calibre (7.62 mm) tripod-mounted piece firing about one hundred rounds a minute in practice, with ammunition supplied in hundred-round drums and a crew of four to six men. It must be stated plainly, however, that neither the Spanish colonial army nor the Katipunan used the Gatling gun in the fighting of 1896. The Spanish service weapons were Mauser-type bolt-action rifles in 7.65 mm, Berthier rifles and older Remington rolling-block rifles, while the backbone of their firepower was 12 and 16 cm field and mountain guns, with steam launches and gunboats providing support on the rivers and along the coast. The insurgents fought with cold steel — bolos and kris — and with captured Mauser and Remington rifles. The forty thousand rifles and forty thousand cartridges bought before the rising never reached the islands, because the British navy stopped the arms-laden steamer Kowshing in the harbour approaches, and although rebels did capture several Spanish mountain guns in the fighting near Manila, they had neither the gun crews nor the spare parts to use them. What actually brought the Gatling gun onto Philippine soil happened three years later: in the Philippine–American War that followed the American expedition of 1899, US artillery brought tripod-mounted Gatling guns forward to cover infantry advancing along roads and across rice fields, and used them in the frontal attacks at Imus, Malabon and in the Bulacan operations. In other words, the weapon on this card stands for the firepower of the next war, not for the reality of August 1896.
tactics: 起事的組織與戰術有三個特點。第一是蓋蒂普南式的宣誓與動員：以割掌取血、合誓的方式吸收會員，在山區設立「卡納爾」的武裝小組作為游擊骨幹，鄉鎮則以「卡帕里坦」維持命令、糧食與情報的傳遞，山民以「信件日」為名沿山嶺遞送消息。第二是象徵與行政層面的破壞：起義者焚燒西班牙的社區稅憑（cedula），廢除殖民政府的門牌與法庭，把教會田產的支配權轉到阿利卡班手上，使西班牙的徵稅與司法在鄉村實際停擺，稅收改由革命政府自徵，充作游擊隊的糧餉與購械。第三是防禦工事：一八九六年末革命軍在帕西格河沿線修築石砌胸牆與「巴拉巴拉漢」野戰陣地，把馬尼拉南方同卡維特隔開；卡維特方向則以民兵依託教堂與修道院據守；西班牙軍隊以炮兵支援的密集步兵縱隊反覆衝擊這些陣地，一八九七年一月才突破帕西格防線。西班牙方面的戰術以縱隊為主軸：從馬尼拉與比克蘭出發的機動縱隊，編制包含步兵營、輔助部隊、炮兵小分隊與工程部隊，靠一八九〇年代已鋪設的電報線與蒸汽輪船調度，在省際公路上縱深推進，再配合以鎮為單位的外圍封鎖與定期掃蕩。一八九六年八月末，萊加斯皮率領的先鋒隊在布拉干、邦板牙方向嘗試連續攻擊，遭鄉村抵抗而被迫撤回；其後西班牙改採穩紮穩打的分省收復，先以縱隊奪回道路與橋樑（例如布拉干省的比納卡揚—達拉希坎橋），再以炮兵覆蓋鄉村堡壘，最後由步兵佔領。河海方向，汽艇沿帕西格河與馬尼拉灣對岸的革命軍陣地實施封鎖與艦炮射擊，切斷陸路補給。
tacticsEn: Three features stand out in the organisation and the method of the rising. First, the Katipunan way of oath and mobilisation: members were taken in by cutting the palm and pledging blood; armed bands called kanals were organised in the mountains as the backbone of the guerrilla war, while in the towns the katiponan kept orders, food and intelligence moving, with upland people carrying messages along the ridges under the name of letter days. Second, the destruction of the colonial administration at the symbolic and administrative level: the insurgents burned the community tax certificates, the ceduIas, voided the Spanish house numbering and the courts, and moved control of church estates over to the alikaban, so that Spanish taxation and justice in the countryside actually stopped working; the money was then collected by the revolutionary government itself and used to feed the guerrillas and to buy arms. Third, field fortifications: towards the end of 1896 the revolutionaries built stone breastworks and palalhahan positions along the Pasig River to cut Manila off from Cavite, and in Cavite the militia held church and convent strongpoints, while Spanish infantry attacked these positions in dense columns under artillery fire and did not break the Pasig line until January 1897. The Spanish method was built around columns: mobile columns leaving Manila and Biak-na-Bato with infantry battalions, auxiliary troops, artillery detachments and engineer units, coordinated along provincial roads by the telegraph lines already laid in the 1890s and by steamships, and combined with cordons drawn around individual towns and periodic sweeps. At the end of August 1896 Legazpi's vanguard tried a series of attacks in Bulacan and Pampanga and was forced back by village resistance; the Spanish then changed to a methodical recovery of the provinces one at a time, taking back roads and bridges first with the columns — the bridge at Binakayan–Dalahican in Bulacan, for instance — then covering the village stockades with artillery, and only then occupying them with infantry. On the rivers and the coast, steam launches blockaded the insurgent positions along the Pasig and on the far side of Manila Bay and shelled them from the water, cutting the landward supply line.
data: 有根據可寫的數字不多，且多數出自敵對雙方的公報，只能作概數看待。起事前蓋蒂普南自報會員約三萬人，分佈於八個以上分會；直接參與首夜起事的人數，通行說法是約三百人，另有數千鄉民在隨後數週加入各支游擊隊。西班牙在菲律賓的常備軍總數在九千至一萬四千人之間（統計口徑差異很大），一八九六年夏馬尼拉都會區一帶可調動的西班牙兵約三千人，另有數千名土著輔助部隊與民兵；一八九七至一八九八年間西班牙再向菲律賓調派約四萬名增援，多方記述都在四萬上下，但船期、訓練與補給不足令大批兵力遲遲未能上陸。首都宣布戒嚴之後，城市與城郊的戰事持續約四個月，主要戰鬥集中在八月二十三日至八月二十九日之間，之後是拉古納、卡維特、八打雁各省逐省拉鋸，布拉干省比納卡揚—達拉希坎橋的戰役在九月中旬結束，一八九六年十一月初塔利薩一戰後，八打雁全省進入軍法管制。關於卡面這件加特林機槍，可靠的數字是：六管、人力搖柄、每分鐘作戰射速約一百發、百發彈鼓、整門槍連三腳架約五六十公斤、需四至六人操作；美軍一八九九年遠征時在菲兵力由一萬餘人增至三萬人上下，總計派兵約十二萬五千人，加特林機槍正是在這批部隊的編制之內。
dataEn: There are not many figures that can be given with confidence, and most of them come from the bulletins of hostile parties, so they can only be treated as approximations. The Katipunan claimed some thirty thousand adherents spread over more than eight chapters before the rising; the number who took part in the first night is usually given as about three hundred, and several thousand more villagers joined the guerrilla bands in the weeks that followed. The Spanish permanent garrison in the Philippines is put at between nine thousand and fourteen thousand men, the figures varying widely with the source and the year, while in the metropolitan area of Manila about three thousand Spanish troops could be mustered in the summer of 1896, alongside several thousand native auxiliaries and constabulary. Between 1897 and 1898 Spain sent a further reinforcement of about forty thousand men, which most accounts place at around that figure, but shortages of shipping, training and supply kept much of it from ever landing. After martial law was declared in the capital, the fighting in the city and its outskirts ran for some four months, with the main clashes concentrated between 23 and 29 August, followed by a provincial war of attrition in Laguna, Cavite and Batangas; the battle for the Binakayan–Dalahican bridge in Bulacan ended in mid-September, and after the action at Talisay in early November 1896 the whole of Batangas province was placed under military control. On the card's Gatling gun the reliable figures are these: six barrels, a hand crank, about one hundred rounds per minute in practice, hundred-round drums, a complete gun and tripod of some fifty to sixty kilograms, and a crew of four to six men. When the Americans landed in 1899 their force in the islands grew from a little over ten thousand men to about thirty thousand, with roughly one hundred and twenty-five thousand men sent out in all, and the Gatling guns were part of the establishment of those units.
cause: 起事有四層直接成因。第一是稅制：一八九四年的人口普查同時大幅上調社區稅憑的稅額，並沿用殖民政府以「襯衣」名義徵收的舊法，向無財產的農民強收現金與牲畜，把大批鄉村家庭推向破產；一八八九年為慶賀西班牙女王伊莎貝拉二世銀婚而徵集的「五十萬比索」專款更是直接抽乾鄉村，錢大多花在馬尼拉的紀念工程上。第二是教產問題：西班牙政府在十九世紀末重新處理教會地產的產權與租佃糾紛，教會在全國握有大片稻田、玉米田與糖業土地，佃農的租約與繼承權屢受行政干預；一八九六年十二月一日總督府頒布的行政重組與教產法令，被民間解讀為政府要進一步把土地讓渡予教團，於是流傳出一份措辭更激烈的同日文書，要求把一切教產立即歸還原主；此文書是否出自博尼法西奧之手、是否本來就不存在，史家至今爭議不休，但它確實成為動員的催化劑。第三是教育與語言：一八九六年馬尼拉大學被要求以西班牙語授課、限制非西班牙人註冊，殖民政府同時擴大對世俗傳教士的迫害，一八七二年三名世俗教士被絞死的舊案在此時仍被反覆引用。第四是改革運動的失敗：宣傳派在馬德里與巴黎遊說十年，得到的只是零星讓步，一八八八至一八九五年間接成立的菲律賓聯盟中，一部分成員正是後來蓋蒂普南的骨幹，於是轉向武裝道路；一八九六年間策劃的軍火購買（步槍四萬支、子彈四萬發）本應讓起事有計劃地進行，英國海軍扣船使計劃落空，革命軍遂在沒有外來槍械的情況下先行舉事。
causeEn: There were four immediate causes behind the rising. The first was taxation: the census of 1894 sharply raised the community tax certificate and kept up the old colonial practice of collecting a camisa tax, taking cash and livestock from peasants who owned nothing and driving large numbers of rural families into ruin; the special levy of five hundred thousand pesos raised in 1889 to celebrate the silver jubilee of Queen Isabella II drained the countryside directly, and most of the money went on commemorative works in Manila. The second was the question of friar lands: towards the end of the nineteenth century the Spanish government reorganised title to church property and the disputes over tenancy, and the Church held great tracts of rice, corn and sugar land while the rights of tenants to their leases and to inheritance were repeatedly set aside by administrative decree. The administrative reorganisation and land decrees promulgated by the governor-general on 1 December 1896 were read in the provinces as the government handing still more land to the religious orders, and a document of the same date with far more radical wording began to circulate, ordering that all church estates be returned to their original owners at once. Whether that document was written by Bonifacio or never existed at all is still disputed by historians, but it certainly acted as a catalyst for mobilisation. The third cause was education and language: the university of Manila was required to teach in Spanish and to restrict the registration of non-Spanish students, and the colonial government at the same time widened its persecution of secular priests, with the 1872 hanging of three secular clergy still being cited. The fourth was the failure of the reform movement: the propagandists had canvassed Madrid and Paris for a decade and won only scattered concessions, and part of the Liga Filipina founded between 1888 and 1895 — among them the future backbone of the Katipunan — turned to arms instead. The arms purchase planned for 1896, forty thousand rifles and forty thousand cartridges, was meant to give the rising a proper schedule, but the British seizure of the ship left the plan without a timetable, and the revolutionaries rose without foreign arms.
impact: 短期看，一八九六年的武裝起事在軍事上是失敗的：西班牙軍在首都周邊與中呂宋逐省收復，蓋蒂普南原有的領導層在一八九六年底至一八九七年五月相繼被處決，革命軍的武裝骨幹退回山區。長期看，這場革命卻決定了菲律賓的命運。它把殖民地的臣民身分徹底否定，創造出以國民而非臣民自我理解的群眾動員能力，使西班牙自由派提出的改革方案（包括一八九六至一八九七年間的自治與菲化方案）失去意義，也讓西班牙國內出現難以擺脫的菲律賓問題。一八九七年九月革命軍在馬拉洛斯召開國民大會並制憲，一八九八年五月馬尼拉的香港會議把革命目標同美軍戰略結合，同年十二月巴黎條約把菲律賓轉讓予美國——此時的菲律賓已不是一個安分的西班牙屬地，而是一個擁有自己憲法與外交主張的政治體。一八九九年爆發的菲美戰爭中，革命軍的組織、宣傳、戰地醫療與後勤動員架構被對方研究與沿用，延伸到後來的數十年。八月二十三日此後成為起義紀念日，一九九九年制定的第九二五五號共和國法把八月最後一個星期一訂為國民英雄日，並明文把一八九六年革命的先驅列為國家英雄，其後再把日期移至八月三十日，與黎剎逝世紀念日合併，於是這場起事成了現代菲律賓國家記憶的座標。
impactEn: In the short run the armed rising of 1896 failed militarily: the Spanish recovered the provinces around the capital and central Luzon one by one, the original Katipunan leadership was executed between the end of 1896 and May 1897, and the armed core of the movement withdrew into the mountains. In the long run, however, the revolution decided the fate of the Philippines. It destroyed the identity of the colony as a subject population, created a mass capacity for mobilisation as a nation rather than as subjects, made the reforms proposed by the Spanish liberals — including the autonomy and Filipinisation schemes of 1896 and 1897 — meaningless, and left Spain with a Philippine question it could not shake. In September 1897 the revolutionaries convened the national assembly at Malolos and drew up a constitution; in May 1898 the conference held in Manila with the Hong Kong junta tied the aims of the revolution to American strategy, and in December the Treaty of Paris transferred the islands to the United States. The Philippines was by then no longer a passive Spanish possession but a polity with its own constitution and its own diplomatic claims. When the Philippine–American War broke out in 1899, the organisation, the propaganda methods and the field medical and logistic arrangements built by the revolutionaries were studied and carried on by the other side, and the structures they created lasted for decades. The 23rd of August became the anniversary of the rising; Republic Act 9255 of 1999 made the last Monday of August National Heroes Day and named the pioneers of the 1896 revolution as national heroes, and a later amendment moved the date to 30 August, merging it with the anniversary of Rizal's death, so that this revolt became a fixed coordinate of modern Filipino national memory.
result: 結果可以分成軍事與政治兩層。軍事上，蓋蒂普南的起事在呂宋中部被西班牙軍逐步壓平：卡維特、八打雁、內湖各省在一八九六年十月至一八九七年一月間陸續收復，馬尼拉帕西格河沿線的野戰陣地在西軍持續炮擊下於一八九七年一月被突破，革命軍退回山區，發動者或戰死、或被處決、或流亡海外；一八九七年五月特耶羅斯會議另立阿吉納爾多為最高領袖，十二月十五日與總督普里莫·德·里維拉簽訂《比亞克—巴塔特條約》，以解散武裝換取大赦與改革讓步，這條約對西班牙政府是鎮壓的收尾，對革命軍卻是一場政治交易；次年一月得知美國願意以二千萬美元買下菲律賓、而西班牙已無力再戰後，阿吉納爾多撕毀條約。政治上，這場革命在西班牙殖民地結束的同時開啟了另一段歷史：西班牙王國的最後一面旗在美軍進入馬尼拉後降下，革命軍自己則在馬洛斯的國民大會上選出總統、頒布憲法，成為亞洲第一部成文憲法的持有者；從起義到共和國的路線，之後又因美軍占領而轉入另一條戰線，菲美戰爭的結局才真正決定了菲律賓在二十世紀的走向。
resultEn: The outcome divides into a military and a political layer. Militarily, the Katipunan rising was gradually crushed in central Luzon: Cavite, Batangas and Laguna were recovered one after another between October 1896 and January 1897; the field positions along the Pasig in Manila were broken by sustained Spanish artillery fire in January 1897; the revolutionaries fell back into the mountains, and those who had started the rising were killed in action, executed or exiled. In May 1897 the Tejeros Convention set up Aguinaldo as supreme, and on 15 December he signed the Pact of Biak-na-Bato with Governor-General Fernando Primo de Rivera, trading the dissolution of the armed bands for amnesty and a promise of reform — for the Spanish government a closing act of pacification, for the revolutionaries a political bargain. In January of the following year, when it became known that the United States was willing to pay twenty million dollars for the islands and that Spain could no longer fight, Aguinaldo tore up the pact. Politically, this revolution ended the Spanish colony and simultaneously opened another chapter of history: the last flag of the Spanish monarchy came down in Manila when the Americans entered, while the revolutionaries themselves elected a president and promulgated a constitution at the Malolos assembly, becoming the holders of the first written constitution in Asia. The line from insurrection to republic was then bent again by the American occupation, and it was the outcome of the Philippine–American War that truly determined the course of the Philippines in the twentieth century.
